research.title: From Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering — Karpathy Calls Time of Death, Now What?
research.whyTrending: Andrej Karpathy (who coined 'vibe coding' in Feb 2025) admitted in 2026 that the era is ending in favor of agentic engineering with specs. Controversial, opinionated, perfect for engagement.

seo.suggestedTitle: Vibe Coding Is Over. Agentic Engineering Is the Job Now

gaps: Most posts recap Karpathy's talk but never show what agentic engineering looks like on a real Tuesday
Nobody quantifies the workflow shift (5-15% code by hand, PEV loop) with concrete practice
No honest 'how do I actually make this shift' section for working devs

facts: Karpathy coined 'vibe coding' Feb 2025; at Sequoia AI Ascent 2026 said 'I've never felt more behind as a programmer'
Dec 2025 = tipping point: agentic tools went from 'helpful but messy' to reliably correct chunks
Software 3.0: LLMs are a new kind of computer; programming shifts from 'writing code' to 'writing context'
'Vibe coding raises the floor; agentic engineering raises the ceiling'
PEV loop (Plan -> Execute -> Verify) replaces 'prompt and hope'
Working agentically: ~5-15% of code written by hand; rest is specs, tests, plan modes, multi-agent
Five core skills: spec design, diff review, eval design, security oversight, quality taste
Karpathy: 'not allowed to introduce vulnerabilities because of vibe coding'; technical depth = bigger multiplier (10x+)
Forbes (Mar 2026): AI agents wrote ~80% of Karpathy's code; concern about the junior-developer ladder

strategy.angle: Not another Karpathy recap. A working dev's honest field guide: what agentic engineering actually looks like day-to-day, the five skills that now pay, and the uncomfortable truth about juniors.
